author: JILL ZIMA BORSKI
title: Key Colony commission discusses grants and golf - NewsBreak
text:
By JILL ZIMA BORSKI ,
5 hours ago
KEY COLONY BEACH — It was clear during the Key Colony Beach City Commission's November meeting that city residents support golf professional Daryl Rice, who maintains the city’s golf course and would like to see his contract extended.
The city also decided to contract with Ron Book for lobbying services for a year at $50,000. For years, Book has represented several governmental entities in the Florida Keys in Tallahassee, especially with regard to budget allocations, said City Administrator John Bartus. He added the city is pursuing grant funds and is to lobby for certain appropriations every year. The city also uses Ballard Partners as lobbyists, he said.
Mayor Freddie Foster said lobbying for grants for wastewater and stormwater improvements is critical.
“(These are) improvements that need to be done to the city,” he said.
Foster said three outfalls of untreated stormwater currently go to the city’s canal system.
“We have plans right now to address one coming up on 7th Street, and then two more on 11th Street. Once they’re done, this city will be the only city in all South Florida that can claim that we have no untreated water going into canals. The only one. Nobody’s even close. What that does is it opens up a whole other world of grants for canal restoration, canal improvements,” he said.
The commission added and approved a proposal for spending $226,600 for membrane replacement at the sewer plant that was recommended by the utility board.
Continuing the lobbying discussion, Foster added, “People like Ron Book … (open) doors that would allow us to get (grant) monies. Because frankly, we can’t afford it. It’s just a fact of life.”
Martha Dreyer, the city’s new code officer, was introduced at the meeting. Staff said she’s been doing a “heck of a job.”
Citizen comments showed widespread support for retaining Rice and continuing his contract with the city. Resident Bill Catto said he has played the KCB golf course for 30 years.
“Keeping Daryl is in the public interest,” he said, adding Rice has a working knowledge of the course and keeps it affordable. Lynn Goodwin, Len Testa and Jimmy Padgett chimed in with support for Rice as well.
The commission subsequently approved a second interim golf course lease agreement extension with Rice.
Regarding resident input, the city has created a place on its website to share ideas. The ideas will go to the city clerk and she, in turn, is to send them on to the beautification committee, the recreation committee, staff or the council.
The city’s meeting was preceded by discussion of a 56-page agreement with contractor Pedro Falcon for city hall renovations and a second agreement with All Aspects Inspections Services for $16,200 for third-party inspections services.
The next city commission meeting is set for Dec. 18 at 9:30 a.m.
